rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before any outcome; synthetic validation on the real gate designs first (A1); replication on all 18 periods with >= 200 idle gates; 3 natives (NE43, blocked spells G27+G51, #focus); 108 estimate rows; confirm.py frozen and dry-run, not run. Missing: the beta_s-by-family split; holdout.
rationale.faithfulness: The starvation model is refuted where it can be tested: in 4/4 powered aging periods the age slope survives every input definition (G51 -0.48 -> -0.53), cross-validation favours trap age (14.9 vs 1.3 nats per 1000 gates), and the starvation slope has the wrong sign. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H0 I1. The negative is clean and well identified (synthetic F2), but the hypothesis's model fails.
rationale.usefulness: Tells an operator that ambient input does not unstick aged idle agents (recent chatter holds them at the gate) and that trap depth must be capped by the scaffold or broken by a directed kick at a gate. Modest: it rules out a lever rather than adding one.

one_line: Trap aging is not input starvation: the age slope survives every input clock (G51 -0.48 -> -0.53), and recent chatter lowers escape (beta_s +0.23).
